morningLede: National active listings built 7% in 30 days (11,497→12,337) yet months-stock fell 13.7→13.4 because the annual sold base grew even faster (10,069→11,070) — this is absorption, not glut. The supply response is landing where prices ran hardest: WA added 21% more listings in a month (607→732) into a 7.9-month market with asking $/m² still rising ($1,000→$1,041), while Sydney's basins remain frozen at 28.7–33.7 months and Victoria's overhang keeps building (16.9→17.1 months, 53% of national stock).
note: House views written each morning by the desk analyst from last night's run. Income and build-cost figures are APPROXIMATE external benchmarks (label them as such, or verify current figures with web search). Land figures are from the certified RLP dataset.

houseViews.view: Updated: the freeze holds but it is stratifying. Sydney Northwest is the pure strike — 33 months of stock, only 191 of 570 listings priced (34%), asking $2,410 vs $2,342/m² sold on the thin priced tail. Sydney Southwest still asks $2,107 against $1,511/m² certified (+39% gap) at 28.7 months, while Sydney South West's priced stock has converged to sold ($2,196 vs $2,084, a 5% gap) yet still sits at 33.7 months on 264 annual sales — proof that honest pricing alone doesn't clear a market this deep. NSW's headline improvement (months-stock 16.5→15.3, $/m² 1,532→1,475) remains mix; capitulation will come via lot compression and incentives, not printed cuts.
houseViews.falsifier: Basin priced-share rising above 60% (Northwest especially) alongside corridor months-stock falling below 20 on rising sold counts.

houseViews.view: Maintained: VIC is 53% of national active listings (6,572 of 12,337) and the overhang is still building — 16.9→17.1 months over 30 days with actives up 6,368→6,572 and Melbourne Peri-Urban at an extreme 38.5 months on just 125 annual sales. But it remains the only deep market that is honestly priced: 95% of listings carry a price and the ask-to-sold gap is a workable 13% ($841 vs $742/m²) versus Sydney's up-to-39%. Cheap ($394k median), abundant, and screenable makes VIC the mechanical landing zone for the late-2026 investor rotation; the overhang caps price growth through mid-2026 but this is digestion, not a freeze.
houseViews.falsifier: VIC months-stock pushing past 20 with sold 12m rolling below ~4,000, or new-listing absorption failing to lift by Q1 2027.

houseViews.view: New: the fallen-angel belt is showing the first evidence that capitulation clears. Torquay's decline is decelerating (-13.5% prior year → -5.9% last 12m) with volume surging to 43 sales in the latest window from 9 three years ago; Winchelsea cut -11.8% and printed 21 sales. Contrast Portarlington (-27.3% over 3yrs on 10 sales) and San Remo (-25.9%) where the adjustment is incomplete. Mechanism: coastal vendors who reprice find a bid — the same medicine Sydney refuses. Position: the bottom in the priced lifestyle names is forming; avoid the ones still holding 2022 rates on single-digit volume.
houseViews.falsifier: Torquay/coastal volumes falling back below ~15 per window, or price declines re-accelerating past -10% in the next windows.

houseViews.view: Maintained: from 1 Jul 2027 negative gearing narrows to new builds and the CGT discount becomes indexation — investors rationally rotate into land from late 2026, and the bid lands where product is priced and cheap: VIC (95% priced, $394k) and outer QLD/SA corridors, not Sydney basins where 66% of Northwest stock cannot even be screened. Tight markets (SA 6.2 months, WA 7.9, Adelaide North 5.4) get the price inflation; loose priced markets get the volume. The national sold base already rising 10% in a month (10,069→11,070 12m-rolling) is consistent with early positioning.
houseViews.falsifier: No pickup in investor-share of land sales or VIC/QLD new-listing absorption by Q1 2027, or policy amendment before commencement.

houseViews.view: Maintained: strong but composition-inflated — headline sold-$/m² growth still carries one estate at roughly a third of 2026 sales, like-for-like ≈ +9.5%. The tightness is genuine: 6.2 months of stock and Adelaide North clearing at ask ($914 asking vs $910 sold $/m², 5.4 months) — a zero-negotiation market. The affordability ceiling remains the central risk: $420k median in the historically cheap state, with price defended via lot compression (Roseworthy -47% lot size over 3yrs, Mount Barker -27%, Morphett Vale -33%) — compression is the market's confession that the gross-price ceiling binds. While stock holds near 6 months the mechanism is deceleration, not correction, and the investor rotation delays the reckoning.
houseViews.falsifier: Stock above 10 months, incentive share rising two runs in a row, or lot compression stalling while sales volumes fall.

houseViews.view: Maintained at high conviction: $/m² is accelerating into the ceiling — +49.7% prior year, +99.6% last 12 months to $1,027/m² (vs $344 three years ago) while lots compressed another 38% in a single year and volume thinned (79→45→35 sales per window). A market doubling its rate while shrinking its product by a third on falling volume is borrowing from the price ceiling, not raising it. Sell stage stock into this rate; do not underwrite englobo at $1,027/m² residuals.
houseViews.falsifier: Lot sizes stabilising while $/m² keeps rising on volume recovering above ~50 sales per window.

houseViews.view: Updated: the supply response has arrived — listings up 21% in 30 days (607→732), the largest proportional build of any state, into a market still tight at 7.9 months with asking $/m² up $1,000→$1,041 and a 20% ask-to-sold gap ($1,041 vs $867). Mandurah is the accelerating rocketship (+24.4% then +98.6% to $842/m², lots -35% over 3yrs) while Hilbert and Australind show fading second derivatives (59→27% and 53→43%). Position: the tight-supply story is intact but vendors are pricing the next leg while developers rush stock to market — the classic late-cycle collision. The easy Perth-metro repricing is done; the marginal dollar chasing satellites is late money.
houseViews.falsifier: WA months-stock rising above 10, or rocketship windows where lot compression continues but sold $/m² growth drops below 10%.

houseViews.view: Maintained: regional VIC majors remain the liquid, stabilised end of Victoria — Bendigo corridor at 8.8 months on 304 annual sales, Ballarat at 10.1 on 458, both roughly half the VIC state average of 17.1 and tighter than any Melbourne fringe corridor. The suburb-level Bendigo fallen-angel print (-37.6% sold $/m²) is 7 sales with lot size simultaneously down 37% — mix, not collapse. The genuine distress lives in Melbourne Peri-Urban (38.5 months) and the Gippsland belt (South Gippsland 33.1 months, Gippsland 26.2).
houseViews.falsifier: Bendigo/Ballarat corridor months-stock rising above 14, or sold volumes falling two consecutive runs.

houseViews.view: Maintained: the QLD state series remains contaminated by the 7-Jul universe expansion (948→1,022 suburbs) — the 30-day 'crash' (asking $539k→$478k, $/m² $1,029→$710, actives 758→1,056) is regional QLD (Townsville $305k/8.8 months, Gympie, Kingaroy) entering the sample, not repricing. Corridor and suburb series say the underlying market is firm: 8.9 months statewide, South Ripley +82% last 12m to $1,774/m², Bahrs Scrub +53% to $1,319. One flag inside the rocketships: Greenbank's +56.6% print sits on just 6 sales versus 76 three years ago — treat as thin, not a trend.
houseViews.falsifier: Like-for-like (pre-expansion suburb set) QLD asking or sold $/m² actually falling on the next monthly comparison.

policyCalendar.event: Negative gearing restricted to NEW BUILDS only; CGT 50% discount replaced by indexation (new-build investors keep choice). Expected to rotate investor demand toward new land/dwellings from late 2026.
